https://www.coventrytelegraph.net/news/c.text: A Coventry MP has said bringing a hit-and-run suspect back to the UK has been a 'long and difficult journey.' Dolars Aleksanders has been charged over the death of 12-year-old Keaton Slater. Keaton was fatally injured after being hit by a BMW on Radford Road in June 2024. Aleksanders, 23, was charged with causing death by dangerous driving after being extradited from Latvia. West Midlands Police said Aleksanders was detained in Latvia in July and flown into Gatwick Airport on Wednesday. He is set to appear at Birmingham Magistrates' Court today (August 6). READ MORE: Young man sexually assaulted by group of men in Nuneaton READ MORE: Dolars Aleksanders charged over death of Keaton Slater in Coventry MP Taiwo Owatemi welcomed Aleksanders' extradition after working with the Slater family on efforts to bring him back to the UK. She also thanked West Midlands Police and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS). Ms Owatemi told CoventryLive : “ Today marks an important moment for the family of Keaton after a long and incredibly difficult journey. My thoughts remain with them, and I would like to thank West Midlands Police , the Crown Prosecution Service, the Latvian authorities, and everyone involved in the international cooperation that has brought the case to this stage. “ Since the death of Keaton, I have been in contact with his family and have raised their concerns with the relevant UK and Latvian authorities throughout this process. I have also continued to support local efforts to improve road safety in his memory. “ As criminal proceedings are now active, it is important that the judicial process is respected while the case proceeds through the courts. ” Ben Samples, from the CPS, said Aleksanders will now face criminal proceedings in relation to the death of Keaton. He added that the 23-year-old has 'the right to a fair trial' and that the judicial process must be respected. Mr Samples said: “ We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendant are active and he has the right to a fair trial. It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary, or sharing of information online which could in any way prejudice these proceedings. ” Sign up for CoventryLive newsletters to stay up to date with the latest news across Coventry and Warwickshire . http://www.euronews.com/2026/09/08/openi.text: North Korea called the first road bridge across its narrow border with Russia a concrete sign of tightening bonds, state media reported on Tuesday, as Pyongyang gains advantages from its powerful neighbours Moscow and Beijing.The bridge over the Tumen river into Russia and an under-construction span to China are part of a shift that offers Western-sanctioned Pyongyang economic and strategic options it has long sought, experts said.North Korea "will simultaneously secure two major overland routes linking it with Russia and China, allowing it to encourage competition between the two countries and maximise its gains," said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University.He noted the bridges also "can be a message to the United States that North Korea has no reason to beg Washington for sanctions relief or make concessions on denuclearisation in order to negotiate," Lim added.Russia noted the bridge is designed to accommodate expanded growth in freight with the capacity for up to 300 vehicles daily, which adds to the rail and air links already between the neighbours.Ukrainian rights group Truth Hounds, however, previously warned that the new bridge could become "a direct artery for moving North Korean troops, construction brigades and military officials into Russia, with Russian technology and resources flowing in the opposite direction."The ceremony on Monday marking the new bridge's opening came as Russia and North Korea have heavily boosted military and economic ties since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.North Korea dispatched thousands of troops to Russia in 2024 to help ward off a Ukrainian incursion into the Kursk region, while Kyiv has accused Moscow of using North Korean missiles in its regular barrages.South Korea's central bank estimated in July that North Korea's economy grew more than 3% for a third straight year in 2025, citing it's expansion of economic cooperation with Russia as a "major drive."The bank's official said North Korea's gross national income also "received a boost from a sharp rise in foreign currency earnings" linked to the deployment of its troops to Russia.Beijing-Moscow-Pyongyang bloc"The completion of the bridge is a significant event adding a new dynamic movement to the overall bilateral cooperation," North Korean official Pak Thae-song said in comments carried by the official KCNA news agency.North Korea and China are already connected by the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which is regularly used by passenger trains, but its capacity is limited.After a long halt, the bridge partly reopened and restored daily passenger train services with China earlier this year, but has not yet resumed issuing tourism visas to Chinese citizens, who once made up the bulk of its overseas visitors.North Korea has long kept tight control over foreign visitors and effectively sealed its borders at the start of the COVID-19 pandemic six years ago.The New Yalu River Bridge, intended as an alternative and eventual replacement of the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, is expected by experts to be completed this year.The completion of the bridge "sends a political and geopolitical message demonstrating the formation of a "North Korea-China-Russia continental triangular bloc," said Lim.

Subscribe There are international windows that offer a little clarity, and then there are the rare ones that leave a team with something close to a statement. Northern Ireland’s four-game Nations League fixtures belonged in the second category: unbeaten, top of League B Group 2, and still without conceding a goal. - Advertisement - That is not a bad way to spend a November break, especially for a young side still learning how to manage the small margins that decide tight games. Michael O'Neill’s team opened with a win away to Georgia, followed it with a 0-0 draw against Hungary at Windsor Park, beat Ukraine in Trnava, and then closed the window with another 0-0 home draw against Georgia. Across the four matches, the defensive record stood out even more than the results themselves. Northern Ireland were the only team in this year’s competition not to concede during the extended four-game run. A defensive run with real meaning That matters because clean sheets in a short tournament stretch are rarely accidental. They usually point to structure, concentration and a group that understands its jobs without the ball. Northern Ireland were not perfect in every phase, but they were consistently hard to break down, and that gave them a platform in every game. In a young squad, that kind of reliability can be more valuable than one flashy win. Shea Charles, who is only 20 and speaking after his fourth cap, said he could not be happier with the window. He said everyone in the country was buzzing, and that feeling was mirrored inside the dressing room. More importantly, he described the group as “really good” and said the team had handled a long spell together with maturity, especially away from home. Charles also pointed to the attacking side of the picture, noting that Northern Ireland created a lot of chances at home and probably more against Georgia than they did against Hungary. The message was not that the attack has been solved. It was that the chances are there, and on another night some of them go in. That is a fair read, because a team can be impressive without being completely polished. - Advertisement - Youth, competition and the next step The longer window also gave O'Neill the chance to use more younger players in an already young squad, and Charles was clear on what that should mean. More games, he said, mean more opportunities to shine. He also stressed that every player who has featured has shown they are capable of starting, which is a healthy problem for any manager to have. That competition should matter in November, when Northern Ireland come back with momentum and expectations a little higher than before. The clean-sheet run will not last forever, and the attack will need to be sharper if they are to keep turning control into wins. But top of the group after four fixtures, with no goals conceded and a squad still growing together, is a strong place to be. For Northern Ireland, the big picture is simple enough: the results say they are competitive, the defensive record says they are organised, and the mood says they believe the best may still be ahead. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq4g.text: Image source, AFP Image caption, Photos of one of the suspected attackers were shared by AFP news agency By Tom Bennett Reporting from Jerusalem Published 23 October 2026, 10:25 BST Updated 26 minutes ago Five Israelis have been wounded and two suspected Palestinian attackers killed by Israeli security forces following a shooting in the occupied West Bank, Israeli officials say. Footage verified by the BBC shows an intense gun battle between soldiers and the gunmen, at a military checkpoint at the entrance to the city of Hebron. In response, Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had ordered the military to prepare for a full lockdown of the West Bank, beginning later on Friday. The attack comes at a time of high tensions, with extremist Jewish settlers targeting Palestinians during the annual olive harvest, and Israel's general election taking place in four days time. The two injured Israelis are in critical condition, according to Israel's ambulance service. The Israeli military said it had found a large quantity of ammunition in the attackers' vehicle. The military said they believe the gunmen had intended to carry out a much larger attack on the nearby Route 35, but ran into the checkpoint - so instead decided to open fire there. Unverified CCTV footage shows two gunmen exit a car armed with what appears to be a handgun and an assault rifle and start firing on soldiers at the checkpoint, before coming under return fire. The Israeli military said it had begun raids on the homes of the attackers, while far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said he had ordered the demolition of several Palestinian buildings adjacent to the site of the attack. It is common practice for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis. Netanyahu, who has built his election campaign on promising security for Israelis, said that his Likud party would cancel campaign events for the morning. The West Bank was already expected to be placed under lockdown for the election on Monday and Tuesday, according to Israeli media. At least 96 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN. Four Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians there over the same period, the UN says.
